kernels.definition: In music, a triad is a set of three notes (or "pitch classes") that can be stacked vertically in thirds.

facts.text: A seventh chord is a chord consisting of a triad plus a note forming an interval of a seventh above the chord's root.

anchor.quote: A seventh chord is a chord consisting of a triad plus a note forming an interval of a seventh above the chord's root.

facts.text: The seventh destabilized the triad, and allowed the composer to emphasize movement in a given direction.

facts.text: There are four different inversions of a seventh chord.

kernels.definition: In music, harmony is the concept of combining different sounds in order to create new, distinct musical ideas.

facts.text: In these genres, chord progressions are the defining feature on which melody and rhythm are built.

anchor.quote: In these genres, chord progressions are the defining feature on which melody and rhythm are built.

facts.text: Chord progressions are the foundation of harmony in Western musical tradition from the common practice era of classical music to the 21st century.

anchor.quote: Chord progressions are the foundation of harmony in Western musical tradition from the common practice era of classical music to the 21st century.

facts.text: A first chord forms a 'progression' with a second chord, and a second with a third.

facts.text: For example, the relative minor of C major is A minor, and in the key of A minor, the i, iv and v chords are A minor, D minor and E minor.

facts.text: In many styles of popular and traditional music, chord progressions are expressed using the name and "quality" of the chords.

mcItems.q: Which description best fits a triad in basic harmony?
op: Three notes stacked vertically in thirds
A triad plus a note a seventh above the root
Four notes arranged in any order
A chord with seven notes total
mcItems.ex: Three notes stacked in thirds matches the definition of a triad. A common misconception is to treat the extra seventh as part of a triad, but that would describe a seventh chord instead.

mcItems.q: How many different inversions does a seventh chord have?
op: Two different inversions
Three different inversions
Four different inversions
Five different inversions
mcItems.ex: A seventh chord has four different inversions. The plausible misconception is to count only the common triad inversions, but the source states that seventh chords have four inversions.

keyTerms.df: A group of three pitch classes arranged by stacking in thirds.
keyTerms.eg: In a simple C-E-G sonority, the notes form a triad.
keyTerms.mi: It is the same thing as a seventh chord.
keyTerms.cx: A seventh chord adds a note forming a seventh above the root, so it is not just a triad.

keyTerms.df: A chord built from a triad with one additional note a seventh above the root.
keyTerms.eg: A chord like C-E-G-B is an example of this type.
keyTerms.mi: It must contain seven notes.
keyTerms.cx: The name refers to the added seventh interval, not to the number of notes in the chord.

mcItems.q: In a Western tonal context, what best describes harmony?
op: Different sounds combined to create distinct musical ideas
A single melody supported only by rhythm
A sequence of silent pauses in a phrase
The written names of individual notes
mcItems.ex: Correct: harmony is the combination of different sounds to create new musical ideas. The likely misconception is to treat harmony as either melody alone or as a list of note names, but the source defines it as sound combination rather than notation or a single line.

mcItems.q: Which example shows a chord progression in A minor?
op: A minor, D minor, E minor
C major, F major, G major
A minor, C major, E major
E minor, A minor, D minor
mcItems.ex: Correct: in A minor, the i, iv, and v chords are A minor, D minor, and E minor. A common misconception is to choose a familiar major-key pattern, but the source gives the minor-key set explicitly.

keyTerms.df: The combination of different sounds that creates distinct musical ideas.
keyTerms.eg: A passage where voices or instruments sound together to form a richer effect.
keyTerms.mi: It means only loud or pleasant-sounding notes.
keyTerms.cx: Harmony is about combining sounds, not just describing volume or liking a chord.

keyTerms.df: A sequence in which one chord leads to another, forming a harmonic pattern.
keyTerms.eg: In A minor, A minor to D minor to E minor is a chord progression.
keyTerms.mi: It is just the written chord names with no musical movement.
keyTerms.cx: The source emphasizes that a first chord moves to a second and then to a third, so progression involves ordered harmonic motion.

mcItems.q: A student hears a short piece that has two sections of about equal length. Which label best fits that description?
op: binary form
through-composed form
strophic form
theme and variations
mcItems.ex: Binary form fits because it is used for a musical piece with two sections that are about equal in length. A common misconception is to choose a form name just because a piece has more than one section; the key evidence here is the two-section, roughly equal-length structure.

mcItems.q: When analyzing a self-contained musical piece or movement, what level of organization is being described?
op: the entire structure of the piece
a single motive or short idea
the balance of sound and silence
one repeated ending pattern
mcItems.ex: The entire structure of the piece is correct because this level concerns the full, self-contained musical piece or movement. A likely misconception is to focus on a small repeated idea or ending pattern, which describes a smaller unit rather than the whole form.

keyTerms.df: The overall structure of a musical composition or performance.
keyTerms.eg: A listener describes how a movement is organized from beginning to end.
keyTerms.mi: It means only the melody line.
keyTerms.cx: Form includes the full structure, not just one element like melody.

keyTerms.df: A pattern built from two sections that are about equal in length.
keyTerms.eg: A dance movement with an A section and a matching B section.
keyTerms.mi: It means any piece with exactly two notes or two measures.
keyTerms.cx: The label refers to two balanced sections, not to the number of notes or measures.
